notes: Hi everyone, we are Merna, Abdullah, and Shankar. Let us walk you through our project.
Monday morning. Merna opens her laptop and sees a new campaign brief from leadership.
Step one is the briefing. Leadership sets the goal, budget, and timeline.
Merna writes the creative brief and hands it off to the design team.
Then she segments the customer base to figure out who to target.
Merna picks which products to feature based on inventory and margins.
She sets the promotional prices, checking every SKU against minimum advertised price rules.
First major handoff. The brief goes from Merna to Abdullah, the senior designer.
Abdullah searches the DAM for product photos that match the campaign theme.
He builds the master ad, the one creative asset everything else gets adapted from.
Legal reviews every word, every price claim, every disclaimer. This step can take days.
Brand team checks that the creative matches the Macys guidelines.
Another handoff. Abdullah sends the approved creative to Shankar for production.
Shankar turns one master ad into 40 regional variants. Ten regions, four placements each.
The finished variants get handed off to the media coordinator for scheduling.
Activation. Emails, social ads, display banners, and in store signage all go live.
The campaign is live. Everyone watches the numbers.
Anna the analyst pulls performance data and runs attribution analysis.
She writes up what worked and what did not. The report goes back to leadership.
That was the ideal version. Now let us talk about what actually happens.
The campaign manager goes on vacation and everything stalls because the knowledge is in her head.
We stepped back and admitted the ideal was a fantasy.
Merna owns five of the ten steps. One person, half the workflow. Classic bottleneck.
Two weeks in, leadership changes the campaign theme. Start over.
160 files with names like final_v2_FINAL. Nobody knows which is current.
Legal sends everything back because a disclaimer is missing. Two more days lost.
A brand changes their minimum price after the creative is approved. Every variant needs updating.
Shankar builds 40 variants, then a typo is found in the master. Redo all of them.
The deadline does not move. The team is in crunch mode.
Rock bottom. The team is exhausted and the launch is in three days.
What if AI could handle the repetitive parts?
We chose Claude as our AI backbone. Not to replace anyone, but to remove the grunt work.

If our Agentic AI platform takes over just the deterministic steps of those campaigns, we establish an operational floor of **$7.42 Billion in annual cost savings**. That is 93 million hours of manual data entry wiped out."

**[The Revenue Ceiling]**
"But cost savings are just the floor. The true value of this AI is acting as a *Revenue Ceiling*. By shrinking a campaign cycle from 8 weeks down to 2 weeks, we unlock agile marketing. Brands can suddenly launch opportunistic campaigns to capture fleeting micro-trends before they vanish. We calculate this agility recovers **$23.84 Billion in lost sales**."

**[The "Mic Drop" Conclusion]**
"Combined, this is a **$31.26 Billion dollar total value creation opportunity**. 

And to capture it, we aren't going to boil the ocean. Our strategic beachhead is to target the **30,000 Mid-Market retailers**. They have the cash to afford high-value software, but they lack the enterprise capital to build it themselves. Our platform gives them an enterprise-grade AI marketing department out of the box."

notes: Milestone 3. We built the real AI coworker.
In M3 we wired the skills together into a system that runs like a real team member.
M2 had 4 standalone skills. M3 added 3 skills and 2 automations chained together, 3 tools, and a 12 document knowledge base.
This diagram shows which skills fire at which workflow step, automatically.
MCP gives Claude the keys to real functions. RAG gives Claude a filing cabinet of company documents.
The live production interface. Each persona sees only their steps.
Compliance pre check catches problems in seconds that used to take days to discover.
The VP gets an AI generated brief card with benchmarks from past campaigns, via RAG.
If the VP says revise, the AI reads the comment, classifies it, and routes it to the right person.
When the VP approves, an approval cascade fires automatically.
The activity feed shows everything the AI is doing. Transparency builds trust.
The chat is now real. Every message goes to a live AI model with RAG grounding.
Behind the scenes: orchestrator picks the skill, pre fetches documents, calls Claude, saves the result.
